metadata.description: Mock response of a proposed AZCOT point-query API. The values are real (read from the AZCOT coverages at the grid cell an API would select); the endpoint, field names and structure are a proposal. See mock_api/README.md in the AZCOT repository.

grid_cell.selection: nearest cell with surface_type = land (seasonal snow)

periods.daily: keys mon_DD (oct_01 ... mar_31, 182 days); each calendar day pools 30 years x 24 hours
periods.monthly: keys oct, nov, dec, jan, feb, mar
periods.seasonal: one value for the whole October-March season

metadata.units_system: US customary: degF, knots, inches, lbf/ft2; shares in %
metadata.source_dataset: AZCOT (ERDC/CRREL TR-26-5, SR-25-2) hourly ERA5, reprocessed by SNAP (preprocess/ in the AZCOT repo); snowfall from SNAP's ERA5 holdings
metadata.coverage_store: Rasdaman. Coverage ids are those of the draft recipes in rasdaman/ (not yet ingested); values here come from the same ingest-ready NetCDF files.
caveats: Values describe a 0.25 degree (~28 km) ERA5 grid cell, not the exact site; valleys and ridges can differ a lot, especially under winter inversions.
AZCOT computed wind chill from SKIN temperature, not the 2 m air temperature TR-26-5 states; over land in January it runs ~3.5 degF colder (AZCOT_DATA_ISSUES.md, issue 10).
Storm-total snowfall loads depend on a storm definition we chose (dry gaps <= 12 h); see snowfall_loads.storm_definition.
Wind is the hourly mean at 10 m; no gusts.

air_temperature.title: 2 m air temperature (ERA5)
air_temperature.description: Daily: lowest / mean / highest of the 720 hourly values (30 years x 24 h) for that calendar day. Monthly and seasonal: lowest of the daily lows, mean of the daily means, highest of the daily highs. min and max are true 30-year records.

wind_chill.title: Wind chill temperature (AZCOT, NWS 2001 formula)
wind_chill.description: Daily: lowest / mean / highest of the 720 hourly values (30 years x 24 h) for that calendar day. Monthly and seasonal: lowest of the daily lows, mean of the daily means, highest of the daily highs. min and max are true 30-year records.
wind_chill.caveat: AZCOT computed wind chill from SKIN temperature, not the 2 m air temperature TR-26-5 states; over land in January it runs ~3.5 degF colder (AZCOT_DATA_ISSUES.md, issue 10).

wind_speed.title: 10 m wind speed, hourly mean (ERA5); no gusts
wind_speed.description: Daily: lowest / mean / highest of the 720 hourly values (30 years x 24 h) for that calendar day. Monthly and seasonal: lowest of the daily lows, mean of the daily means, highest of the daily highs. min and max are true 30-year records.

snow_depth.title: Snow depth (ERA5-Land, 0.1 degree grid)
snow_depth.description: Daily: lowest / mean / highest of the 720 hourly values (30 years x 24 h) for that calendar day. Monthly and seasonal: lowest of the daily lows, mean of the daily means, highest of the daily highs. min and max are true 30-year records.
snow_depth.caveat: The source is missing hours 01-23 UTC of the last day of every month; those days rest on 30 hourly values instead of 720.

snow_load.title: Snow load of the snowpack on a flat surface, SWE[in] x 5.2 (TR-26-5 eq. 4)
snow_load.description: Daily: lowest / mean / highest of the 720 hourly values (30 years x 24 h) for that calendar day. Monthly and seasonal: lowest of the daily lows, mean of the daily means, highest of the daily highs. min and max are true 30-year records.

freeze_thaw_days.title: Freeze-thaw days per year (hourly air temperature both below and above 32 degF on the same day)

design_cold.description: Air temperature exceeded on the cold side by 1 / 5 / 10% of hours (MIL-HDBK-310 convention), from the monthly 1 degF histograms (value = bin upper edge).

ar70_38_design_type.basis: lowest monthly 1% value; C1 >= -25, C2 >= -50, C3 >= -60, C4 >= -70 degF (AR 70-38 / TR-26-5 Table 1)

atp_cold_zone.basis: ATP 3-90.96 Table 1-3 / TR-26-5 Table 2 zone of the coldest-month mean (typical), the lowest monthly 1% value (design) and the 30-year record low (record)

exceedance.description: Share of hours (%) beyond each threshold. Monthly and seasonal for every variable; daily as well where a daily coverage exists (wind chill, snow load). Histogram-based values are exact to the 1-unit bin; any other threshold can be computed from the *_hour_counts coverages.

wind_chill_at_or_below.caveat: AZCOT computed wind chill from SKIN temperature, not the 2 m air temperature TR-26-5 states; over land in January it runs ~3.5 degF colder (AZCOT_DATA_ISSUES.md, issue 10).

frostbite.title: Frostbite danger levels (TR-26-5 Tables 4-5)
frostbite.description: Time to frostbite of exposed, dry cheek skin, computed for every hour from 2 m air temperature and 10 m wind with TR-26-5 Eq. 5 (Nelson et al. 2002), then counted per danger level. Uses air temperature (not AZCOT's skin-temperature wind chill). Eq. 5 does not reproduce every value of TR-26-5 Table 5.

none.label: No frostbite danger
none.minutes: FT > 120, or air temperature >= 23.36 degF (Eq. 5 undefined)

shortest_time_to_frostbite.description: Shortest time to frostbite in any hour of 30 years (true minimum)

snowfall_loads.title: Snowfall design loads (TR-26-5 section 1)
snowfall_loads.description: From ERA5 hourly snowfall (SNAP ERA5 holdings), water equivalent x 204.7 lbf/ft2 per m. Tentage must carry 10 lbf/ft2 from one 24-hour snowfall; rigid shelters 20 lbf/ft2 from one storm, cleared between storms. A 'year' is the Jan-Mar plus Oct-Dec of one calendar year.
snowfall_loads.storm_definition: Our choice (TR-26-5 gives none): hours with snowfall >= 0.1 mm water equivalent, dry gaps of at most 12 h inside one storm; total from first to last wet hour, credited to the day the storm ends.

sf24_max.title: Record 24-hour snowfall load (largest trailing 24-hour snowfall in 30 years)

sf24_mean_annual_max.title: Mean over 30 years of each year's largest 24-hour snowfall load

sf24_ge10_years.title: Years with at least one 24-hour load >= 10 lbf/ft2 (tentage)

sf24_ge10_days.title: Days per year whose largest 24-hour load is >= 10 lbf/ft2

storm_mean_annual_max.title: Mean over 30 years of each year's largest storm total

storm_ge20_years.title: Years with at least one storm total >= 20 lbf/ft2 (rigid shelters)

storm_ge20_per_year.title: Storms per year with a total >= 20 lbf/ft2

sf72_max.title: Record 72-hour snowfall load (needs no storm definition)

sf72_mean_annual_max.title: Mean over 30 years of each year's largest 72-hour load

climate_limit_verdicts.title: Climate-limit verdicts
climate_limit_verdicts.description: OK / Caution / No for each environmental design limit in the threshold catalog (site_characterization/thresholds.csv): structure snow and snowfall loads, structure wind rating, and vehicle type versus snow depth. Equipment, clothing, fuel and other item verdicts are not included.

legend.OK: The 30-year record never reaches the limit in that month.
legend.CAUTION: The record reaches the limit, but rarely: in at most 1% of the month's hours (MIL-HDBK-310 / AR 70-38 design convention), or, for the single-event snowfall loads, in at most 10% of years.
legend.NO: The limit is reached more often than that.
legend.N/A: Not meaningful at this cell (e.g. snow load on a glacier cell).

% of hours with snow depth above the limit

items.item: Wheeled 4x4 or greater with snow chains

% of hours with snow depth above the limit

items.basis: No upper limit (over-snow vehicles are the answer where snow is deeper than 40 in)

items.notes: Largest trailing 24-hour snowfall (ERA5 hourly snowfall, SNAP holdings); OK = never reached in 30 years, caution = reached in <= 10% of years, no = more often

items.item: Temporary rigid shelters / portable hangars (20 lb/ft2 from a multi-day storm)

limit.test: one storm total at or above the limit

items.notes: Storm-total snowfall (wet hours >= 0.1 mm w.e., dry gaps <= 12 h, see preprocess step 10); OK = never reached in 30 years, caution = reached in <= 10% of years, no = more often
